proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\) and \(1\leq \ell\leq L\), and put
\[
p_{\ell}=(r_{\ell1},r_{\ell2},r_{\ell3},r_{\ell4}).
\]
By the common-rarity assumption, \(p_{\ell j}=\rho c_{\ell j}\).  The coefficient box and rarity-scale assumptions imply
\[
0<p_{\ell j}\leq 4\rho\leq \frac14.
\]
Moreover, for every \(i,j\in J\),
\[
\frac{p_{\ell i}}{p_{\ell j}}
=\frac{c_{\ell i}}{c_{\ell j}}
\leq \frac{4}{1/2}=8.
\]
Thus \(p_{\ell}\in\mathcal P_0\).  By the published identification proposition and the definition of \(G\),
\[
\Delta_{\ell}
=H(r_{\ell1},r_{\ell2},r_{\ell3})-r_{\ell4}
=G(p_{\ell}).
\tag{1}
\]
This step relates the causal contrast \(\Delta_{\ell}\) to the observed-law functional \(G\); it does not define the former as the latter.

Set \(\beta=\alpha/L\).  Since \(0<\alpha<1\) and \(L=15\), one has \(0<\beta<1\); since \(\alpha\) is rational, so is \(\beta\).  We next verify that the coverage and diameter conclusions of the rational outer-interval argument apply for every positive rational \(\eta\), including \(\eta>1/n\).  This avoids invoking the stated pairwise theorem outside its displayed range.

For one pair, abbreviate \(n_j=n_{\ell j}\), \(K_j=K_{\ell j,n}\), \(x_j=K_j/n_j\), and \(M_n=\sum_{j=1}^4n_j\).  In the rational algorithm, the likelihood threshold \(t_{\rm lo}\) is strictly positive.  For every \(\eta>0\), there exists a positive rational mesh \(h\) satisfying
\[
M_nh\leq t_{\rm lo}/4,
\qquad
L_{\rm lip}h\leq\eta/8.
\tag{2}
\]
Hence the finite construction and its deterministic image-containment argument remain valid without the restriction \(\eta\leq1/n\): every \(p\in\mathcal R_\beta(K)\) lies in a retained feasible box, and the global Lipschitz enlargement and outward rounding give
\[
G\{\mathcal R_\beta(K)\}
\subseteq \mathsf{Outer}_{\beta,\eta}(K).
\tag{3}
\]
Indeed, the likelihood Lipschitz inequality used by that construction is
\[
|L_K(p)-L_K(p')|\leq M_n\lVert p-p'\rVert_\infty,
\]
so the first inequality in (2) ensures retention, while the second bounds the image enlargement.  Neither step requires an upper bound on \(\eta\).

Under Bernoulli role sampling and disjoint-role independence, the four counts for this pair are independent binomials with parameters \((n_j,p_{\ell j})\).  For \(0<p_{ell j}<1\), the elementary Bernoulli-divergence bound gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}\!\left\{\operatorname{Bern}(x_j),
\operatorname{Bern}(p_{\ell j})\right\}
\leq \frac{(x_j-p_{\ell j})^2}
{p_{\ell j}(1-p_{\ell j})}.
\]
Because
\[
\mathbb E_{p_\ell}(x_j-p_{\ell j})^2
=\frac{p_{\ell j}(1-p_{\ell j})}{n_j},
\]
the definition of the deviance yields
\[
\mathbb E_{p_\ell}D_{p_\ell}(K)
\leq 2\sum_{j=1}^4 n_j
\frac{p_{\ell j}(1-p_{\ell j})/n_j}
{p_{\ell j}(1-p_{\ell j})}
=8.
\tag{4}
\]
Markov's inequality, the definition of \(\mathcal R_\beta\), and (3) therefore imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Pr_{p_\ell}\{G(p_\ell)\notin I_\ell\}
&\leq \Pr_{p_\ell}\{p_\ell\notin\mathcal R_\beta(K)\}\\
&=\Pr_{p_\ell}\{D_{p_\ell}(K)>8/\beta\}\\
&\leq \beta=\frac{\alpha}{L}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]

For completeness, the diameter calculation also remains valid for arbitrary \(\eta>0\).  Put \(q'=8/\beta+2\log4\).  The likelihood-threshold and mesh inequalities in (2) imply that every feasible point in a retained box belongs to
\[
\mathcal R'(K)=\{p\in\mathcal P_0:D_p(K)\leq q'\}.
\]
The Hellinger lower bound for Bernoulli divergence then gives, for \(p\in\mathcal R'(K)\),
\[
|\sqrt{p_j}-\sqrt{x_j}|
\leq \sqrt{\frac{q'}{2n_j}}.
\tag{6}
\]
Consequently, for any \(p,p'\in\mathcal R'(K)\),
\[
|p_j-p'_j|
\leq 4\sqrt{x_j}\sqrt{\frac{q'}{2n_j}}
+\frac{2q'}{n_j}.
\tag{7}
\]
The global Lipschitz bound, the enlargement in (2), and the final outward rounding therefore give a finite constant \(C_{0,\beta}\), independent of \(\ell,n,\rho,c\), such that
\[
\operatorname{diam}(I_\ell)
\leq C_{0,\beta}
\left\{
\sum_{j=1}^4\left(\sqrt{\frac{x_j}{n_j}}+\frac1{n_j}\right)+\eta
\right\}.
\tag{8}
\]
If the retained list is empty, the returned interval is \([0,0]\), so (8) is still true.  Jensen's inequality, common rarity, the coefficient upper bound, and the lower role-share bound give
\[
\mathbb E_{p_\ell}\sqrt{x_j}
\leq\sqrt{p_{\ell j}}
\leq2\sqrt\rho,
\qquad
n_j\geq\underline\pi n.
\tag{9}
\]
Taking expectations in (8) and using (9), uniformly over the fixed pairs, produces a finite constant \(C_\beta\), depending only on \(\beta\) and the fixed role-share bounds (with the fixed Lipschitz certificate absorbed), for which
\[
\mathbb E_{p_\ell}\{\operatorname{diam}(I_\ell)\}
\leq C_\beta\left\{
\sqrt{\frac\rho n}+\frac1n+\eta
\right\}
\leq C_\beta\left\{
\frac{\max(1,\sqrt{n\rho})}{n}+\eta
\right\}.
\tag{10}
\]
Thus both conclusions needed below hold for every positive rational \(\eta\).

Let \(A_\ell=\{\Delta_\ell\notin I_\ell\}\).  Cross-pair independence is unnecessary: by (1), (5), and the union bound,
\[
\Pr\{\Delta_\ell\in I_\ell\text{ for every }1\leq\ell\leq L\}
=1-\Pr\!\left(\bigcup_{\ell=1}^L A_\ell\right)
\geq1-\sum_{\ell=1}^L\Pr(A_\ell)
\geq1-L\frac{\alpha}{L}
=1-\alpha.
\tag{11}
\]
Write \(I_\ell=[L_\ell,U_\ell]\).  On the simultaneous event in (11),
\[
L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^L L_\ell
\leq L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^L\Delta_\ell
=\overline\Delta
\leq L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^L U_\ell.
\]
By the definition of \(\overline I\), this is precisely \(\overline\Delta\in\overline I\), and hence
\[
\Pr\{\overline\Delta\in\overline I\}\geq1-\alpha.
\tag{12}
\]
Finally, the same definition gives the deterministic identity
\[
\operatorname{diam}(\overline I)
=L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^L\operatorname{diam}(I_\ell).
\tag{13}
\]
Taking expectations in (13), applying (10) to each of the fixed \(L=15\) pairs, and setting \(C_\alpha=C_{\alpha/L}\) proves
\[
\mathbb E\{\operatorname{diam}(\overline I)\}
\leq C_\alpha\left\{
\frac{\max(1,\sqrt{n\rho})}{n}+\eta
\right\}.
\]

Fix \(M>0\). By the definition of \(\Phi\), for any \(a<b\),
\[
 \Phi(b)-\Phi(a)=\int_a^b\phi(w)\,dw>0,
\]
because the declared standard-normal density satisfies \(\phi(w)>0\). Thus \(\Phi\) is strictly increasing. The same positivity gives
\[
 \Phi(-M)=\int_{-\infty}^{-M}\phi(w)\,dw>0.
\]

Assumption \(\rho_n\to0\) implies that, for this fixed \(M\), there is an integer \(n_M\) such that
\[
 4\rho_n<\Phi(-M)\qquad\text{for every }n\ge n_M.
\]
For every \(1\le\ell\le L\), \(j\in J\), and \(n\ge n_M\), the common-rarity equality and the coefficient-box bounds yield
\[
 0<r_{\ell j,n}=\rho_n c_{\ell j,n}
 \le 4\rho_n<\Phi(-M).
\]
Here the strict lower bound uses \(\rho_n>0\) and \(c_{\ell j,n}\ge1/2\). The declared type of \(r\) also gives \(r_{\ell j,n}<1\), so \(q(r_{\ell j,n})\) is well defined. Since \(q=\Phi^{-1}\) and \(\Phi\) is strictly increasing, the preceding display gives
\[
 q(r_{\ell j,n})<-M.
\]
Using the defining formula for the standard-normal density and \(M>0\), we consequently obtain, simultaneously over the finite set of roles and pairs,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 0<\phi(q(r_{\ell j,n}))
 &=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}
   \exp\!\left\{-\frac{q(r_{\ell j,n})^2}{2}\right\}\\
 &\le \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-M^2/2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(L=15\) and \(J=\{1,2,3,4\}\), taking the maximum gives
\[
 0\le
 \max_{1\le\ell\le L,\,j\in J}\phi(q(r_{\ell j,n}))
 \le \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-M^2/2}
 \qquad(n\ge n_M).
\]
Given \(\varepsilon>0\), choose \(M>0\) so large that \((2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-M^2/2}<\varepsilon\), and then use the associated \(n_M\). This proves
\[
 \max_{1\le\ell\le L,\,j\in J}\phi(q(r_{\ell j,n}))\longrightarrow0.
\]

Suppose, toward a contradiction, that some \(C\in(0,\infty)\) satisfied
\[
 \inf_{\ell,j,n}\phi(q(r_{\ell j,n}))\ge \frac1C.
\]
Then \(1/C>0\), and for every \(n\),
\[
 \max_{1\le\ell\le L,\,j\in J}\phi(q(r_{\ell j,n}))
 \ge \frac1C,
\]
contradicting the convergence just proved. Hence no such uniform constant exists.

It remains to connect the exceedance probabilities in this proposition to the cell CDF values appearing in the cited regularity condition. Since \(\phi\) is the standard-normal density, it is even and integrates to one. A change of variables therefore gives, for every \(x\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 \Phi(-x)=\int_{-\infty}^{-x}\phi(w)\,dw
 =\int_x^\infty\phi(v)\,dv
 =1-\Phi(x).
\]
Strict monotonicity of \(\Phi\) then implies, for every \(p\in(0,1)\),
\[
 q(1-p)=-q(p),
 \qquad
 \phi(q(1-p))=\phi(-q(p))=\phi(q(p)).
\]
For each role cell, the CDF probability at the fixed threshold is \(1-r_{\ell j,n}\), because the events \(\{Y\le y_0\}\) and \(\{Y>y_0\}\) are complements. Thus a positive lower bound for the normal-link density at all of those transformed CDF values would imply the same lower bound for \(\phi(q(r_{\ell j,n}))\), uniformly in \(\ell\), \(j\), and \(n\). The cited statement of Djuazon and Tsyawo's Assumption 5 requires precisely such a positive uniform link-density bound. The contradiction above therefore places the whole comparable-rarity triangular sequence outside that regularity regime. Finally, this is a boundary failure and not an exact-zero failure: for every finite \(n\), the already established inequality \(r_{\ell j,n}\ge\rho_n/2>0\) holds in every cell.

added_lemmas.statement: Djuazon and Tsyawo's Assumption 5 requires, among its regularity conditions, a finite constant \(C>0\) that uniformly bounds the working-link density away from zero at every transformed cell CDF value.

source.verbatim_statement: Assumption 5 (Regularity). \(\Phi:\mathbb R\to[0,1]\) is continuously differentiable, with derivative \(\phi(b):=\frac{d}{db}\Phi(b)\). Moreover, there exists a constant \(C\in(0,\infty)\) such that \(\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}\phi(x)\le C\) and \(\inf_{(g,t)\in\mathcal G\times[-T:T]}\inf_{y\in\mathcal Y}\phi(\Phi^{-1}(F_{gt}(y)))\ge1/C\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from Assumption 5 on page 16 of arXiv:2408.07842v2; mathematical typography was rendered in TeX.

proposed.statement: For the standard-normal link, every comparable-rarity triangular array satisfying \(r_{\ell j,n}=\rho_n c_{\ell j,n}\), \(c_{\ell j,n}\in[1/2,4]\), and \(\rho_n\to0\) obeys \(\max_{1\le\ell\le L,\,j\in J}\phi(q(r_{\ell j,n}))\to0\). Hence no constant \(C\) with \(0<C<\infty\) can make \(\inf_{\ell,j,n}\phi(q(r_{\ell j,n}))\ge1/C\), so Djuazon and Tsyawo's Assumption 5 excludes the entire comparable-rarity sequence rather than merely failing at an exact zero cell.
proposed.justification: This locates the rare experiment outside the published interior theorem by the exact regularity inequality used in that theorem.
proposed.gap: Djuazon and Tsyawo's Assumption 5 states the positive link-density lower bound; this proposition records its direct implication for the comparable-rarity array and carries no independent novelty claim.
proposed.consumer: The Gaussian and product-Poisson frontier statements can be read as boundary results on a domain that the published weak-convergence theorem does not cover.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the directly verified published regularity condition as a cited proof dependency and add the target's exact free-symbol closure.
